description: Declared mutants of world_asset (docs/architecture/target/v2/asset.zh-Hant.md; declaration docs/architecture/target/v2/asset-declaration.zh-Hant.md, sections 9, 10 and 30.3): the scenario, view and summary tests, one 'add that member' mutant per compile-failure sample, and the hash of 5.9.1 (AS-6). Each guards a Design Invariant of the formal page (guards 'asset AS-n') or a rule of the declaration. Run: python3 -B tests/common/mutation/run_mutations.py --build-dir build/target/_build/core --catalog tests/common/world_asset/mutations.json --cmake <cmake>

mutants.what: (4) the apply System pulls the view again in the middle of the frame (a second mount at PostUpdate): a System later in the same frame sees a job that finished in that frame
guards: asset-declaration 5.6 一幀之內看到同一份
mutants.cases: view: a job that finishes in the middle of a frame*

mutants.what: (8) the view does not compare lives: an older view gives the old life's Loaded (and value) for a Handle of a newer life
mutants.find: if (record != nullptr && record->life == body->life) return record;
mutants.cases: view: an older view against a newer life*

mutants.what: a Handle's hash also writes the store's internal index of its entry: two catalogs listing the entries in different orders give different Summaries
mutants.find:
void HashValue(Sink& sink, const Handle<T>& handle) {
    HashValue(sink, handle.Id());

mutants.what: (10) a Handle gets State(): the AS-11 sample HANDLE_STATE compiles
a Handle gets Get(): the AS-11 sample HANDLE_GET compiles
AssetRequests gets State(handle): the AS-11 sample REQUESTS_STATE compiles
AssetRequests gives its store: the AS-11 sample REQUESTS_STORE compiles
AssetView::Get gives a writable T*: the AS-10 (a) sample VIEW_GET_WRITABLE compiles
AssetView gets a mutating member (Replace): the AS-10 (a) sample VIEW_MUTATION compiles
mutants.replace:
[[nodiscard]] std::vector<Asset::FailureRecord> Failures() const { return snapshot_.Failures(); }
    void Replace(Asset::AssetSnapshot snapshot) { snapshot_ = std::move(snapshot); }

mutants.what: AssetView becomes copy assignable: the AS-10 (a) sample VIEW_COPY_ASSIGN compiles
AssetView's constructor becomes public: the AS-10 (a) sample VIEW_CONSTRUCT compiles
world_asset makes a store for each World (the catalog kept in the Product's buffer): two Worlds decode the same id apart and read different objects
mutants.cases: scenario: two Worlds of a Product share one store*

mutants.what: the prepare function does not run maintenance first: a DropOldFirst replacement's old World's drops are not taken before the new World requests, so an id held only by the old World is revived instead of read again
the apply System does not run maintenance: an id no World holds stays alive
world_asset registers no OnDestroy: the store is not stopped at the Product's end, and the unfinished job is not counted as discarded while the Product's buffer is there
the prepare function puts an empty view in the World: beforeSwap sees Queued for what is loaded
the apply System rebuilds a removed view empty instead of from the store
mutants.cases: view: an AssetView an author removed*

mutants.what: WaitingForLoader counts as finished in Ready and Unfinished (design review r4)
mutants.replace:
return state == Asset::AssetState::Loaded || state == Asset::AssetState::Failed ||
           state == Asset::AssetState::WaitingForLoader;
mutants.cases: view: a Handle waiting for its loader*

mutants.what: a request-level failure leaves the group complete (design review r5)
AssetView::Get does not check the C++ type: a value of another type with the same type name is read as T (design review r9)
mutants.cases: view: Get reads a value only as the C++ type*

mutants.what: a Handle the view has not seen leaves dependenciesFinished true (design review r10)
mutants.cases: view: an older view against a newer life*

mutants.what: Build ignores WorldAssetOptions: a World with the skeleton off that names its own apply schedule fails to build (design review r20)
mutants.cases: view: a World with the skeleton off*

mutants.what: Handle::Body() becomes public: the AS-11 sample HANDLE_BODY compiles
mutants.find: // The body (the strong core or the request-level failure), through Detail::HandleAccess only.
mutants.replace:
public:
    // The body (the strong core or the request-level failure), through Detail::HandleAccess only.

mutants.what: Handle::Life() becomes public (Body() stays private): the AS-11 sample HANDLE_LIFE compiles
mutants.find:
// The life of the asset this Handle holds; 0 without a core. Through Detail::HandleAccess only.
    [[nodiscard]] std::uint64_t Life() const noexcept { return body_ ? body_->life : 0; }
